results.title: On the power of the conditional likelihood ratio and related tests for weak-instrument robust inference - ScienceDirect
results.content: # On the power of the conditional likelihood ratio and related tests for weak-instrument robust inference. Power curves of the Conditional Likelihood Ratio () and related tests for testing in linear models with a single endogenous variable, , estimated using potentially weak instrumental variables have been presented for two different designs. The fixed- design changes these endogeneity features with changing values of in a way that makes it less suitable for an analysis of the behaviour of the tests in low to moderate endogeneity settings, or when and the correlation of the structural and first-stage errors, , have the same sign. At larger values of , the fixed- design implicitly selects values for where the power of the test is high. In fixed- design Monte Carlo simulations, we find that Liml- and Fuller-based conditional Wald tests and the Fuller-based conditional test are more powerful than the test when the degree of endogeneity is low to moderate.

Use the new **estat weakrobust** command to perform reliable inference on endogenous regressors.
